title: BBC World News | Saudi Arabia: Cruise Missiles and Drones Intercepted
gist: CNAS fellow Becca Wasser tells BBC World News that Saudi Arabia is struggling to defend itself against cruise missile and drone attacks; the page also lists CNAS work warning that the Iran war has drained US interceptor stocks.

insights.claim: Becca Wasser of CNAS says Saudi Arabia is struggling to defend itself against incoming cruise missiles and drones.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Watch Gulf air-defence demand and Saudi vulnerability as a driver of interceptor and counter-drone procurement.

insights.claim: A CNAS report summary states that the war with Iran has taken a heavy toll on the US munitions stockpile, with over half of its inventory of high-end missile interceptors consumed.
insights.speaker: Carlton Haelig
insights.so_what: Supports a multi-year munitions replenishment cycle in the FY2027 defense budget.
insights.quote: Over half its inventory of high-end missile interceptors has be
insights.locator: More from CNAS: Munitions Procurement and the Fiscal Year 2027 Defense Budget

insights.claim: CNAS commentary warns that if full-scale fighting resumes against a reconstituted Iran, coalition forces would run out of Patriot, THAAD and Standard Missile interceptors in days.
insights.speaker: Stacie Pettyjohn & Philip Sheers
insights.so_what: Interceptor scarcity argues for higher production rates and cheaper counter-drone options; watch prime contractors in these programs.
insights.quote: coalition forces will run out of Patriot, THAAD, and Standard Missile interceptors in days
insights.locator: More from CNAS: How to Avoid Disaster in the Next Iran War

insights.claim: A CNAS podcast frames missiles and drones as slow missiles that provide the bang in airpower, and asks what US magazines must look like to defend Taiwan given usage in Iran.
insights.speaker: Stacie Pettyjohn & Philip Sheers
insights.so_what: Magazine depth, not platform count, becomes the binding constraint for a Taiwan contingency.
insights.quote: Missiles and drones (slow missiles) put the bang in airpower.
insights.locator: More from CNAS: We Go High, We Go Low

insights.claim: A CNAS commentary argues sea drones are a Taiwan game changer, as China prefers to win without firing a shot in its bid to strangle Taiwan's strategic autonomy.
insights.speaker: Trey Meeks
insights.so_what: Unmanned maritime systems are a growth area in Taiwan defense spending.
insights.quote: China prefers to win without firing a shot
insights.locator: More from CNAS: Sea Drones a Taiwan Game Changer
